codeReview.summary: Clean module split of launa-sim/src/spa_sim.rs into config.rs (182 lines), state.rs (101 lines), frame_gen.rs (335 lines), and physics.rs (153 lines). mod.rs retains SpaSim struct, all public methods, and 157 inline tests. Delegation pattern is correct: SpaSim methods are thin wrappers that delegate to sub-module functions. Public API is identical — launa-integration-tests compiles without changes. All 157 launa-sim tests pass, all 904+ workspace tests pass.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The architecture.md documents that 'launa-sim is NOT #![no_std]' but doesn't mention the internal module structure of launa-sim/spa_sim (config, state, frame_gen, physics). After this split, the architecture doc should be updated to describe the module organization within spa_sim.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: architecture.md only describes launa-sim at the crate level without mentioning the new sub-modules of spa_sim/

sharedStateObservations.observation: The sub-modules frame_gen and physics are declared as 'pub mod' in mod.rs but contain only 'pub(crate)' items. This is functionally fine (external code can see the module but not its items), but a 'pub(crate) mod' declaration would be more precise. This is a minor style observation, not a bug.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: mod.rs lines 10-13 declare 'pub mod config;', 'pub mod frame_gen;', 'pub mod physics;', 'pub mod state;' — config and state have truly public types (re-exported via 'pub use'), while frame_gen and physics have only 'pub(crate)' items.

summary: PASS. The split-launa-sim feature cleanly modularizes spa_sim.rs into 4 focused modules with proper delegation, preserving the full public API. All 157 tests pass inline in mod.rs. launa-integration-tests compiles without import changes. No behavioral changes, no duplication introduced. Module boundaries are clean: config structs → config.rs, state types → state.rs, frame generation → frame_gen.rs, physics model → physics.rs. Two minor observations: (1) architecture.md could document the new module structure, (2) frame_gen/physics modules could use 'pub(crate) mod' instead of 'pub mod' for more precise visibility.
